From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of the Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Headline view

The Seller's package is not "fair and balanced." Several of its provisions work together to remove most of the Buyer's protection:

1. **General disclosure** of the whole data room and public records,
2. a **Buyer-knowledge bar** that includes constructive knowledge ("discoverable"),
3. **all limitations applied to all Claims**, including title, tax, indemnities and potentially fraud, and
4. a **20% cap** that also covers title and capacity.

Taken together, almost every known risk in this deal would fall outside any remedy. That includes Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, the bonuses, the data incident and Sandbar. The Buyer would then have a capped, time-limited claim only for risks nobody has found yet.

The cover note also contradicts the Seller's own Disclosure Letter on several points (see section C). Nothing in the cover note should be relied on unless it is converted into a warranty, condition or indemnity.

**Quantifiable known exposures already exceed AUD 4.1m before on-costs.** That is about 86% of the proposed AUD 4.8m cap:

| Item | Amount (AUD) |
|---|---|
| Riverlark facility | ~3,200,000 |
| DD-005 bonuses (excl. payroll tax, super, on-costs) | 420,000 |
| Sandbar renewals | 330,000 |
| Ironquay SOW3 open fees | 180,000 |
| **Subtotal** | **~4,130,000** |
| Plus unquantified: Bluefen (~30% of revenue), DD-006 privacy incident, Ironquay IP ownership | — |

---

## A. Limitation regime (Clauses 8.3, 9.3, 12, 13, 20.5)

### 1. General cap of 20% (AUD 4.8m), Cl 12.1
- **Issue:** The cap is at the low end for a deal where material known risks are being pushed into the warranty regime. If title and tax are capped at 4.8m, the Buyer bears 80% of the price at risk on matters the Seller controls entirely.
- **Push back:**
  - The general warranty cap should be 30–50%, or 20% only if W&I insurance sits above it.
  - Title, capacity and solvency warranties should be capped at 100% of the price (plus costs).
  - The tax indemnity should be capped at 100%.
  - Specific indemnities should sit outside the general cap.

### 2. De minimis AUD 25k and basket AUD 250k as a deductible, Cl 12.2
- **Issue:** The basket is about 1.04% of the price and works as a deductible ("only the excess"). The Buyer would absorb the first AUD 250k of loss, plus every claim under AUD 25k.
- **Push back:**
  - Use a tipping basket, so recovery runs from the first dollar once the threshold is reached.
  - Set the basket at about 0.5% (~AUD 120k) and the de minimis at about AUD 10k.
  - Aggregate related or recurring claims for de minimis purposes.
  - Thresholds should not apply to title, tax, specific indemnities, leakage or covenant claims.

### 3. Time limits, Cl 12.3 / 13: "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"
- **Issue:** This default rule is a trap. It extends the 18-month window, cap and thresholds to every claim not expressly carved out: indemnities, tax, title, covenants, restraints and completion obligations. Any drafting gap would favour the Seller.
- **Push back:**
  - **Reverse the default.** Limitations should apply only to "General Warranty Claims" as defined.
  - 18 months for general warranties is acceptable, or 24 months to cover two audit cycles.
  - Tax: at least 5–7 years, or the relevant ATO/OSR amendment period plus 6 months.
  - Title/capacity: at least 6 years. That aligns with the contract limitation period under the *Limitation Act 1969* (NSW), and the period is longer if the SPA is executed as a deed.
  - Specific indemnities (privacy, IP): periods tailored to each risk, generally 3–6 years.

### 4. Fundamental warranties treated like general ones "for administrative simplicity"
- **Reject outright.** Title is the core of the bargain. If the shares are not validly held, the Buyer has paid AUD 24m for a capped claim of AUD 4.8m. "Administrative simplicity" is not a commercial reason.

### 5. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature", Cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5
- **Issue:** As drafted, this could be argued to cover fraud, wilful concealment and dishonest disclosure, as well as indemnities and price mechanics.
- **Push back:**
  - Carve out fraud, dishonesty, wilful misconduct and deliberate concealment by the Seller or its agents. Excluding liability for fraud is generally contrary to public policy, but say so expressly.
  - Exclusive remedy must not limit specific performance, injunctions, termination rights, completion and price adjustment, leakage, or covenant enforcement.
  - Non-reliance should be limited to statements outside the SPA and Disclosure Letter. It must not undercut the warranties.
  - Note the interaction with *Australian Consumer Law* s 18. Non-reliance clauses are evidentiary only and do not fully exclude statutory liability. Even so, the Seller will use this to defend misleading or deceptive conduct claims, so the Buyer should not concede it more broadly than necessary.

### 6. Buyer knowledge, Cl 8.3
- **Issue:** This is the most damaging provision. It bars any claim about matters known to the Buyer or *its advisers*, or *discoverable* from the data room or public records. That is constructive knowledge on top of general disclosure, and it would effectively cancel the warranties. It also creates an incentive to under-read the data room.
- **Push back:**
  - Replace it with a clause stating that the Buyer's knowledge (actual, constructive or imputed) does not reduce any claim, except to the extent a matter is **Fairly Disclosed** in the Disclosure Letter.
  - Fallback: limit it to the actual knowledge of named deal-team individuals, and exclude advisers.

---

## B. Disclosure Letter

### 7. General disclosure of the entire data room and public registers, DL 1.1–1.2
- **Issue:**
  - Wholesale disclosure of the data room, Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" is not fair disclosure.
  - Paragraph 1.2 adds that general disclosure operates "without limiting" specific disclosure, so the specific paragraphs are not the outer limit.
  - The data room cut-off is 22 September 2026. Today is 5 November 2026, so anything after that date is unaddressed.
- **Push back:**
  - Only specific disclosures count, and only if **Fairly Disclosed**: with enough detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature, scope and likely financial effect of the matter.
  - If any data room disclosure is conceded, limit it to a scheduled, indexed and archived copy (USB or hash) provided to the Buyer, and to documents specifically cross-referenced against a warranty.
  - Delete "publicly searchable corporate records." At most, allow the results of specified ASIC, PPSR and court searches as at a stated date.
  - Seller updates to disclosure between signing and Completion must not cure breaches. Any material new matter should give the Buyer a termination right.

### 8. Non-admission and "no conclusion" language, DL 1.4 and 11
This is acceptable as a reservation, but it confirms that each specific paragraph flags a risk without resolving it. Under the Seller's regime these items become disclosed, and therefore unclaimable. **Every disclosed item below must be addressed through a condition, price mechanism, completion deliverable or specific indemnity, not through warranties.**

---

## C. Specific matters: where the cover note contradicts the Disclosure Letter

| Item | Seller cover note | Disclosure Letter |
|---|---|---|
| Bluefen | "addressed" | No final consent; conditions not shown satisfied |
| Riverlark | release "following Completion" | Not repaid; no discharge |
| DD-006 | "not expected to be material" | Scope, access and notification status all unknown; no loss stated |
| Sandbar | "ordinary-course" | Does not state whether ordinary course, terminable or accrued |
| Ironquay | indemnity "adequate" | No payment receipt or confirmatory assignment |

### 9. Bluefen change-control consent (~30% of FY26 revenue), Cl 3 / 6.3
- **Issue:**
  - "Reasonable endeavours" is a weak obligation.
  - The proposal treats the condition as satisfied on delivery of *a* written consent, even if the clause 11.3 conditions are not met or the consent is itself conditional.
  - Losing Bluefen would remove about AUD 3.6m of revenue, roughly 30% of a business of about AUD 12m revenue, and with it a large part of the valuation.
- **Push back:**
  - Make it a **Condition Precedent**: unconditional written consent from Bluefen in a form satisfactory to the Buyer, with evidence that all clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied or waived, and not withdrawn by Completion.
  - Only the Buyer may waive it.
  - The Seller should use all reasonable endeavours or best endeavours, with a long-stop date and a Buyer walk right.
  - Consider either a price adjustment or escrow linked to Bluefen retention for 12 months, or a specific indemnity if Bluefen terminates in reliance on change of control.

### 10. Riverlark facility (~AUD 3.2m), Cl 2 / 7
- **Issue:** On a debt-free/cash-free basis, this is Financial Indebtedness that must be repaid at Completion. A release "following Completion" leaves:
  - the security in place over a company the Buyer now owns,
  - a likely change-control default under clause 8.1 when the shares transfer, and
  - the Buyer's financiers unable to take clean security.
- **Push back:**
  - Before Completion, deliver a payoff letter stating the exact payout amount and per-diem interest.
  - At Completion, deliver an executed deed of release, PPSR financing change statements or an authority to lodge them, and the return of title documents.
  - The payout should come from the purchase price through the funds flow and be deducted as Debt.
  - The Seller should obtain a waiver of clause 8.1 for the period up to Completion.
  - Add an indemnity for any Riverlark amounts or break costs.

### 11. DD-005 Completion bonuses (AUD 420k plus on-costs), funds flow
- **Issue:** The Seller says these are "a matter for the Seller" but leaves them out of the funds flow. The **Company is the employer**, so the Company bears the cost, which is the Buyer's cost after Completion. The letter is silent on:
  - payroll tax (NSW),
  - superannuation guarantee, depending on whether the bonus is ordinary time earnings,
  - PAYG withholding, and
  - workers' compensation premiums.

  The continued-employment conditions also mean some payments may fall due after Completion.
- **Push back:**
  - Define the bonuses and all associated taxes and on-costs as Transaction Expenses or Debt, deducted dollar-for-dollar from the price.
  - Itemise them in the funds flow and pay them through Company payroll at or after Completion from a retained amount.
  - Add a specific indemnity for any shortfall.
  - Confirm there are no other change-of-control or retention payments.

### 12. Ironquay IP, Cl 11.1 (indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment)
- **Issue:** The real risk is not the AUD 180k fee. Under DD-004 clause 7.3, ownership of the SOW3 Project Materials transfers only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. Until then, the Company may not own IP it relies on. That exposes it to infringement claims, injunctions, re-development costs and loss of customers. Note also that the AUD 180k "open" figure in DD-010 is not bank-verified.
- **Push back:**
  - **Completion deliverables:** evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees, from the Seller's account or deducted from the price; an executed confirmatory deed of assignment from Ironquay; and moral rights consents if relevant.
  - Add a specific indemnity covering all Loss from any Ironquay ownership, infringement or payment claim, including re-development and third-party claims. It should sit outside the general cap, basket and 18-month limit, with a 4–6 year period.
  - The IP warranties should not be "settled under the general regime."

### 13. DD-006 export/privacy incident (~1,240 records), Cl 4.6 / Sch 6
- **Issue:**
  - A download link containing personal information (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) went to an unintended external recipient.
  - Access, scope and notification are all unresolved. Under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme (*Privacy Act 1988* (Cth), Pt IIIC), an entity that suspects an eligible data breach must complete an assessment within 30 days. Since the matter was still "preliminary" at 22 September, that deadline may already have passed. Check the date of awareness.
  - With revenue around AUD 12m, the Company is unlikely to qualify for the small business exemption.
  - The Privacy Act penalty and enforcement regime was strengthened in 2024, and a statutory privacy tort now exists.
  - Customer contracts, possibly including Bluefen's, may carry their own incident-notification obligations.
- **Push back:**
  - **Pre-Completion covenants:** finish the assessment, obtain an independent forensic report shared with the Buyer, make any OAIC or individual notifications, comply with customer contract notifications, and follow a remediation plan agreed with the Buyer.
  - Add a **specific indemnity** for all Loss from the incident: regulatory, third-party, customer, remediation and notification costs. It should sit outside the cap and thresholds, run for 3–4 years, and be supported by escrow.
  - Add specific privacy and data security warranties.
  - Reject the label "not expected to be material."

### 14. Sandbar renewals (3 × AUD 110k = AUD 330k)
- **Issue:** The disclosure itself tells the Buyer to read DD-008 and DD-011 "together for timing/scope." That raises the question of whether a single commitment was split to fall below an approval threshold, or whether Sandbar is related to the Seller.
- **Push back:**
  - **Diligence:** obtain the contracts and approvals, confirm Sandbar's ownership and any link to Harbourglass, and check whether the renewals are terminable without penalty and whether they are prepaid or accrued.
  - **SPA:**
    - Add a warranty that the renewals were entered on arm's-length terms in the ordinary course and are terminable.
    - Include any accrued or prepaid amounts in the working capital or debt definitions.
    - If Sandbar is related to the Seller, treat the renewals as leakage or Debt and require termination at Completion.
    - Add a conduct-of-business covenant requiring Buyer consent for commitments above a set amount between signing and Completion.

### 15. Title (DD-012 share register)
- **Issue:** A share register is only prima facie evidence (*Corporations Act* s 176). The Disclosure Letter expressly says the Buyer has not verified title, and the Seller wants title capped at AUD 4.8m.
- **Push back:**
  - **Diligence:** ASIC company extract and historical searches, share certificates, the constitution, all issue and transfer documents, PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company, and confirmation that there are no options, convertibles, ESOP awards or SAFEs. This last point matters with a VC seller.
  - **SPA:** title, capacity and "no other securities" warranties uncapped or capped at 100% of the price, running at least 6 years.
  - **Completion deliverables:** executed transfers, original certificates, resignations, and waivers of pre-emptive rights.

### 16. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
- **Issue:** The Seller says notification only for the lease and no consent for Mossvale. These are the Seller's characterisations, given without any warranty.
- **Push back:**
  - Have counsel independently review both clauses, especially any deemed-assignment or change-in-control definitions.
  - Add a warranty that no consents are triggered by the transaction other than those listed.
  - Add a covenant to give the lease notification on time.
  - Request the landlord's acknowledgment and, if prudent, a Mossvale comfort letter.

### 17. Tax, "settled under the general regime"
- **Reject.** Require:
  - a standalone tax indemnity for pre-Completion taxes, including payroll tax on the DD-005 bonuses,
  - no de minimis or basket,
  - a cap of 100% of the price, and
  - a time limit of 5–7 years, or the amendment period plus 6 months.
- Also include the usual conduct-of-claims and gross-up provisions.

---

## D. Structural protection: security for recovery

Harbourglass Ventures is a VC seller and will likely distribute the proceeds. Warranty and indemnity claims are only worth what can be recovered. Recommend:
- **Escrow or retention** of about 10–15% of the price (AUD 2.4–3.6m) for 18–24 months, with a separate longer escrow for the privacy and IP indemnities. Alternatively, a parent or fund guarantee.
- **W&I insurance** as an option. However, W&I excludes known and disclosed matters, so it does **not** replace the specific indemnities, conditions and deductions above.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Buyer position |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap 20% | 30–50% (or 20% with W&I); title, capacity and tax at 100% |
| 2 | Thresholds | Tipping basket ~AUD 120k; de minimis ~AUD 10k; related claims aggregated; none for title, tax or indemnities |
| 3 | Time limits / "applies to all Claims" | Reverse the default; 18–24 months general; tax 5–7 years; title 6+ years; tailored indemnity periods |
| 4 | Fundamentals capped like generals | Reject |
| 5 | Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance | Carve out fraud, concealment, indemnities, covenants, price mechanics and equitable relief |
| 6 | Buyer knowledge, Cl 8.3 | Delete; knowledge doesn't reduce claims except for Fairly Disclosed matters |
| 7 | General disclosure | Specific, fair disclosure only; no public records or whole data room; no curative updates |
| 8 | Bluefen | Buyer-waivable CP: unconditional consent with 11.3 satisfied; best endeavours; long-stop; retention escrow or indemnity |
| 9 | Riverlark | Repay at Completion from price; payoff letter, deed of release and PPSR releases as Completion deliverables |
| 10 | Bonuses | AUD 420k plus all on-costs as Transaction Expenses deducted from price; in funds flow; indemnity |
| 11 | Ironquay | Payment evidence and confirmatory assignment as Completion deliverables; full uncapped-style IP indemnity |
| 12 | DD-006 incident | Complete NDB assessment and forensics pre-Completion; specific indemnity outside the cap; escrow; privacy warranties |
| 13 | Sandbar | Diligence on related-party status and splitting; warranty; leakage or Debt treatment if related |
| 14 | Title | Independent verification; title warranties at 100% of price for 6+ years |
| 15 | Lease / Mossvale | Independent review; no-other-consents warranty; notification covenant |
| 16 | Tax | Standalone indemnity outside the general regime |
| 17 | Recovery | Escrow 10–15% and/or guarantee; W&I only as a supplement |

**Negotiation priority:** Items 6, 7, 5 and 3 come first, because they decide whether any other protection has value. Next are 9, 10 and 8, which affect price and deal certainty. Then 11, 12 and 4, followed by the rest.

**Caveats:**
- This review is based only on the Seller's cover note and Disclosure Letter. I have not seen the full SPA text or the underlying DD-002 to DD-012 documents. Clause references and characterisations should be checked against those documents.
- The statutory points (Privacy Act NDB timing, NSW payroll tax, limitation periods, s 176) should be confirmed by the responsible NSW-qualified lawyer before the mark-up goes out.
- I'd recommend asking the Seller for the post-22 September data room additions and the DD-006 incident timeline now.

That is constructive knowledge on top of general disclosure, and it would effectively cancel the warranties. It also creates an incentive to under-read the data room.
- **Push back:**
  - Replace it with a clause stating that the Buyer's knowledge (actual, constructive or imputed) does not reduce any claim, except to the extent a matter is **Fairly Disclosed** in the Disclosure Letter.
  - Fallback: limit it to the actual knowledge of named deal-team individuals, and exclude advisers.

## B. Disclosure Letter

### 7. General disclosure of the entire data room and public registers, DL 1.1–1.2
- **Issue:**
  - Wholesale disclosure of the data room, Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" is not fair disclosure.
  - Paragraph 1.2 adds that general disclosure operates "without limiting" specific disclosure, so the specific paragraphs are not the outer limit.
  - The data room cut-off is 22 September 2026. Today is 5 November 2026, so anything after that date is unaddressed.
- **Push back:**
  - Only specific disclosures count, and only if **Fairly Disclosed**: with enough detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature, scope and likely financial effect of the matter.
  - If any data room disclosure is conceded, limit it to a scheduled, indexed and archived copy (USB or hash) provided to the Buyer, and to documents specifically cross-referenced against a warranty.
  - Delete "publicly searchable corporate records." At most, allow the results of specified ASIC, PPSR and court searches as at a stated date.
  - Seller updates to disclosure between signing and Completion must not cure breaches. Any material new matter should give the Buyer a termination right.

### 8. Non-admission and "no conclusion" language, DL 1.4 and 11
This is acceptable as a reservation, but it confirms that each specific paragraph flags a risk without resolving it. Under the Seller's regime these items become disclosed, and therefore unclaimable. **Every disclosed item below must be addressed through a condition, price mechanism, completion deliverable or specific indemnity, not through warranties.**

## C. Specific matters: where the cover note contradicts the Disclosure Letter

| Item | Seller cover note | Disclosure Letter |
|---|---|---|
| Bluefen | "addressed" | No final consent; conditions not shown satisfied |
| Riverlark | release "following Completion" | Not repaid; no discharge |
| DD-006 | "not expected to be material" | Scope, access and notification status all unknown; no loss stated |
| Sandbar | "ordinary-course" | Does not state whether ordinary course, terminable or accrued |
| Ironquay | indemnity "adequate" | No payment receipt or confirmatory assignment |

### 9. Bluefen change-control consent (~30% of FY26 revenue), Cl 3 / 6.3
- **Issue:**
  - "Reasonable endeavours" is a weak obligation.
  - The proposal treats the condition as satisfied on delivery of *a* written consent, even if the clause 11.3 conditions are not met or the consent is itself conditional.
  - Losing Bluefen would remove about AUD 3.6m of revenue, roughly 30% of a business of about AUD 12m revenue, and with it a large part of the valuation.
- **Push back:**
  - Make it a **Condition Precedent**: unconditional written consent from Bluefen in a form satisfactory to the Buyer, with evidence that all clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied or waived, and not withdrawn by Completion.
  - Only the Buyer may waive it.
  - The Seller should use all reasonable endeavours or best endeavours, with a long-stop date and a Buyer walk right.
  - Consider either a price adjustment or escrow linked to Bluefen retention for 12 months, or a specific indemnity if Bluefen terminates in reliance on change of control.

### 10. Riverlark facility (~AUD 3.2m), Cl 2 / 7
- **Issue:** On a debt-free/cash-free basis, this is Financial Indebtedness that must be repaid at Completion. A release "following Completion" leaves:
  - the security in place over a company the Buyer now owns,
  - a likely change-control default under clause 8.1 when the shares transfer, and
  - the Buyer's financiers unable to take clean security.
- **Push back:**
  - Before Completion, deliver a payoff letter stating the exact payout amount and per-diem interest.
  - At Completion, deliver an executed deed of release, PPSR financing change statements or an authority to lodge them, and the return of title documents.
  - The payout should come from the purchase price through the funds flow and be deducted as Debt.
  - The Seller should obtain a waiver of clause 8.1 for the period up to Completion.
  - Add an indemnity for any Riverlark amounts or break costs.

### 11. DD-005 Completion bonuses (AUD 420k plus on-costs), funds flow
- **Issue:** The Seller says these are "a matter for the Seller" but leaves them out of the funds flow. The **Company is the employer**, so the Company bears the cost, which is the Buyer's cost after Completion. The letter is silent on:
  - payroll tax (NSW),
  - superannuation guarantee, depending on whether the bonus is ordinary time earnings,
  - PAYG withholding, and
  - workers' compensation premiums.

  The continued-employment conditions also mean some payments may fall due after Completion.
- **Push back:**
  - Define the bonuses and all associated taxes and on-costs as Transaction Expenses or Debt, deducted dollar-for-dollar from the price.
  - Itemise them in the funds flow and pay them through Company payroll at or after Completion from a retained amount.
  - Add a specific indemnity for any shortfall.
  - Confirm there are no other change-of-control or retention payments.

### 12. Ironquay IP, Cl 11.1 (indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment)
- **Issue:** The real risk is not the AUD 180k fee. Under DD-004 clause 7.3, ownership of the SOW3 Project Materials transfers only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. Until then, the Company may not own IP it relies on. That exposes it to infringement claims, injunctions, re-development costs and loss of customers. Note also that the AUD 180k "open" figure in DD-010 is not bank-verified.
- **Push back:**
  - **Completion deliverables:** evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees, from the Seller's account or deducted from the price; an executed confirmatory deed of assignment from Ironquay; and moral rights consents if relevant.
  - Add a specific indemnity covering all Loss from any Ironquay ownership, infringement or payment claim, including re-development and third-party claims. It should sit outside the general cap, basket and 18-month limit, with a 4–6 year period.
  - The IP warranties should not be "settled under the general regime."

### 13. DD-006 export/privacy incident (~1,240 records), Cl 4.6 / Sch 6
- **Issue:**
  - A download link containing personal information (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) went to an unintended external recipient.
  - Access, scope and notification are all unresolved. Under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme (*Privacy Act 1988* (Cth), Pt IIIC), an entity that suspects an eligible data breach must complete an assessment within 30 days. Since the matter was still "preliminary" at 22 September, that deadline may already have passed. Check the date of awareness.
  - With revenue around AUD 12m, the Company is unlikely to qualify for the small business exemption.
  - The Privacy Act penalty and enforcement regime was strengthened in 2024, and a statutory privacy tort now exists.
  - Customer contracts, possibly including Bluefen's, may carry their own incident-notification obligations.
- **Push back:**
  - **Pre-Completion covenants:** finish the assessment, obtain an independent forensic report shared with the Buyer, make any OAIC or individual notifications, comply with customer contract notifications, and follow a remediation plan agreed with the Buyer.
  - Add a **specific indemnity** for all Loss from the incident: regulatory, third-party, customer, remediation and notification costs. It should sit outside the cap and thresholds, run for 3–4 years, and be supported by escrow.
  - Add specific privacy and data security warranties.
  - Reject the label "not expected to be material."

### 14. Sandbar renewals (3 × AUD 110k = AUD 330k)
- **Issue:** The disclosure itself tells the Buyer to read DD-008 and DD-011 "together for timing/scope." That raises the question of whether a single commitment was split to fall below an approval threshold, or whether Sandbar is related to the Seller.
- **Push back:**
  - **Diligence:** obtain the contracts and approvals, confirm Sandbar's ownership and any link to Harbourglass, and check whether the renewals are terminable without penalty and whether they are prepaid or accrued.
  - **SPA:**
    - Add a warranty that the renewals were entered on arm's-length terms in the ordinary course and are terminable.
    - Include any accrued or prepaid amounts in the working capital or debt definitions.
    - If Sandbar is related to the Seller, treat the renewals as leakage or Debt and require termination at Completion.
    - Add a conduct-of-business covenant requiring Buyer consent for commitments above a set amount between signing and Completion.

### 15. Title (DD-012 share register)
- **Issue:** A share register is only prima facie evidence (*Corporations Act* s 176). The Disclosure Letter expressly says the Buyer has not verified title, and the Seller wants title capped at AUD 4.8m.
- **Push back:**
  - **Diligence:** ASIC company extract and historical searches, share certificates, the constitution, all issue and transfer documents, PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company, and confirmation that there are no options, convertibles, ESOP awards or SAFEs. This last point matters with a VC seller.
  - **SPA:** title, capacity and "no other securities" warranties uncapped or capped at 100% of the price, running at least 6 years.
  - **Completion deliverables:** executed transfers, original certificates, resignations, and waivers of pre-emptive rights.

### 16. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
- **Issue:** The Seller says notification only for the lease and no consent for Mossvale. These are the Seller's characterisations, given without any warranty.
- **Push back:**
  - Have counsel independently review both clauses, especially any deemed-assignment or change-in-control definitions.
  - Add a warranty that no consents are triggered by the transaction other than those listed.
  - Add a covenant to give the lease notification on time.
  - Request the landlord's acknowledgment and, if prudent, a Mossvale comfort letter.

### 17. Tax, "settled under the general regime"
- **Reject.** Require:
  - a standalone tax indemnity for pre-Completion taxes, including payroll tax on the DD-005 bonuses,
  - no de minimis or basket,
  - a cap of 100% of the price, and
  - a time limit of 5–7 years, or the amendment period plus 6 months.
- Also include the usual conduct-of-claims and gross-up provisions.

## D. Structural protection: security for recovery

Harbourglass Ventures is a VC seller and will likely distribute the proceeds. Warranty and indemnity claims are only worth what can be recovered. Recommend:
- **Escrow or retention** of about 10–15% of the price (AUD 2.4–3.6m) for 18–24 months, with a separate longer escrow for the privacy and IP indemnities. Alternatively, a parent or fund guarantee.
- **W&I insurance** as an option. However, W&I excludes known and disclosed matters, so it does **not** replace the specific indemnities, conditions and deductions above.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Buyer position |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap 20% | 30–50% (or 20% with W&I); title, capacity and tax at 100% |
| 2 | Thresholds | Tipping basket ~AUD 120k; de minimis ~AUD 10k; related claims aggregated; none for title, tax or indemnities |
| 3 | Time limits / "applies to all Claims" | Reverse the default; 18–24 months general; tax 5–7 years; title 6+ years; tailored indemnity periods |
| 4 | Fundamentals capped like generals | Reject |
| 5 | Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance | Carve out fraud, concealment, indemnities, covenants, price mechanics and equitable relief |
| 6 | Buyer knowledge, Cl 8.3 | Delete; knowledge doesn't reduce claims except for Fairly Disclosed matters |
| 7 | General disclosure | Specific, fair disclosure only; no public records or whole data room; no curative updates |
| 8 | Bluefen | Buyer-waivable CP: unconditional consent with 11.3 satisfied; best endeavours; long-stop; retention escrow or indemnity |
| 9 | Riverlark | Repay at Completion from price; payoff letter, deed of release and PPSR releases as Completion deliverables |
| 10 | Bonuses | AUD 420k plus all on-costs as Transaction Expenses deducted from price; in funds flow; indemnity |
| 11 | Ironquay | Payment evidence and confirmatory assignment as Completion deliverables; full uncapped-style IP indemnity |
| 12 | DD-006 incident | Complete NDB assessment and forensics pre-Completion; specific indemnity outside the cap; escrow; privacy warranties |
| 13 | Sandbar | Diligence on related-party status and splitting; warranty; leakage or Debt treatment if related |
| 14 | Title | Independent verification; title warranties at 100% of price for 6+ years |
| 15 | Lease / Mossvale | Independent review; no-other-consents warranty; notification covenant |
| 16 | Tax | Standalone indemnity outside the general regime |
| 17 | Recovery | Escrow 10–15% and/or guarantee; W&I only as a supplement |

**Negotiation priority:** Items 6, 7, 5 and 3 come first, because they decide whether any other protection has value. Next are 9, 10 and 8, which affect price and deal certainty. Then 11, 12 and 4, followed by the rest.

**Caveats:**
- This review is based only on the Seller's cover note and Disclosure Letter. I have not seen the full SPA text or the underlying DD-002 to DD-012 documents. Clause references and characterisations should be checked against those documents.
- The statutory points (Privacy Act NDB timing, NSW payroll tax, limitation periods, s 176) should be confirmed by the responsible NSW-qualified lawyer before the mark-up goes out.
- I'd recommend asking the Seller for the post-22 September data room additions and the DD-006 incident timeline now.
